newsitem.title: CANADA: WIC vote should stand, Oppenheimer says.
newsitem.headline: WIC vote should stand, Oppenheimer says.

text.p: Oppenheimer & Co said Thursday that the vote count on its motion to dissolve WIC Western International Communications Ltd should stand despite an error in counting at the broadcaster's annual meeting.

The trust company that counted the votes Wednesday said today it made a mistake in counting the ballots. Rather than 57 percent votes of Class B shareholders voting in favor of the motion, only 45 percent were actually in favor, it said.
The revision did not change the outcome of the vote because the motion was defeated by WIC's Class A shareholders. It required two-thirds approval by both A and B shareholders.

Oppenheimer said that under rules of proper procedure for the meeting the original vote as read Wednesday should remain valid. "We're saying that legally that vote should stand," said Oppenheimer managing director Eric Rosenfeld.

Oppenheimer, which proposed the resolution, said WIC was attempting to "circumvent the proper rules of procedure." Even under the new numbers, 62 percent of WIC's B shareholders independent of the controlling stockholders voted in favor of dissolution, the firm said.

"Regardless of the picture that WIC is now attempting to draw, the fact remains that there has been a massive vote of no confidence by WIC's public shareholders with respect to its corporate governance situation," Rosenfeld said.
"We will see if the company has received the message sent by its independent shareholders by monitoring its actions and the fulfillment of its promises in the near future," he said.

WIC said that despite the revision it would still take shareholder concerns seriously. The 57 percent vote in favor of the motion surprised WIC officials on Wednesday and was seen as a sign of discontent among shareholders over the company's performance.
